subject: ventures/window-tinting-bid-calculator
professional: an owner-operator of an auto window tinting shop (IWFA-style film installer) who quotes jobs daily and buys film by the roll

evidence.correctness: Ran: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture dir -> 107 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed by hand and against a throwaway script calling calc.mjs. (1) Default full kit: sqft 2*4+2*3.5+2*1.4+9.5=27.3, x1.15 waste=31.395, x$5.50=172.67 film; minutes 24+24+32+40=120 -> 2h x $28=$56; direct 172.67+56+12=240.67; /(1-0.35)=370.27. Matches calc output 370.265. (2) Front two doors, dyed: 8 sqft x1.15 x1.75=16.10, 24 min=$11.20, +$12 = 39.30; /0.65=60.46 -> floored to $120 minimum. Matches. (3) Default job dyed with removal: removal 2*8+2*8+2*10+30=82 min, total 202 min, price 248.01. Matches. Margin-on-price formula (cost/(1-m)) is the correct convention. Input checks run: 3 front doors rejected, 'Ceramic' (case) rejected, 1.5 rejected. Arithmetic is right; the rate constants are the author's ballpark figures, not from a cited standard (see domain).
evidence.completeness: Checked each README/page claim: pane-count pricing (works), film tier (3 tiers, works), waste factor (works), old-tint removal with slower rear windshield (works, 30 min vs 8), mobile fee, booth overhead, margin + minimum floor (works), flat-per-vehicle comparison/gap (works, pricingGap), printable customer proposal with deposit split (proposal.mjs, 492 lines, tested), usage counter with opt-out (usage.mjs). Two companion landing pages exist and have tests. No TODO/stubs found. Not covered and not claimed: front windshield / sun strip, sunroof, 3rd-row or van glass (quarter max 4, no roll-width logic).
evidence.verification: Ran the full suite: 107 tests pass. Seeded mutation in calc.mjs: changed priceAtMargin from directCost/(1 - margin) to directCost/(1 + margin); 8 tests failed (99 pass, 8 fail), so core pricing is guarded. Reverted with git checkout calc.mjs; re-ran: 107 pass, git status clean. Tests include hand-verified breakdowns with the arithmetic in comments, page-text tests and worked-example-table tests. Weakness: tests were written by the author from the same constants, so they cannot catch a wrong constant (e.g. film cost/sqft); only one mutation tried.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (188 lines) fully and skimmed proposal.mjs exports. calc.mjs is small, frozen constants, single number() validator with integer/max checks, pure functions, clear comments. Defects: blank numeric input silently becomes 0 because '' is not nullish for ??, then Number('')=0 passes min 0 (I ran installerRate:'' and got a price with zero labor, 284.11 vs 370.27, no error); removeOldTint uses Boolean() so the string 'false' is truthy; wasteFactorPercent has no upper bound; removal is all-or-nothing (cannot strip only some panes, though the FAQ says removal is 'only needed on the panes that already have tint').
evidence.claims: Backed: pricing method, margin convention, privacy/no-upload (README, index.html, usage.mjs, usage tests), VLT-not-checked disclaimer present on page, README, proposal. 'Nearly $200' ceramic vs dyed spread on a seven-window job: I computed 31.395 sqft x (5.50-1.75)/0.65 = $181, so roughly supported. Not backed: 'that is how the trade actually prices this work day to day' and the '$180 sedan / $220 SUV' list are unsourced, and VENTURE.yaml lists all three hypotheses as untested with checked: null. Defects: llms.txt links point at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of https://marisstella.app/ (README and VENTURE.yaml use marisstella.app); sitemap.xml and robots.txt reference https://example.invalid/ (may be rewritten at deploy, I did not verify the built output). README test command (node --test ventures/.../*.test.mjs from repo root) is fine.
evidence.fitness: Walked a shop owner's job: pick panes, film, rates, get a price, compare to flat rate, print a proposal with deposit and signature line. That flow works end to end and the proposal is a real extra. Gaps a tint shop would hit in the first hour: no front windshield strip/visor or sunroof, no vehicle presets (user must know pane counts), no film-roll width or linear-foot waste, no per-pane removal choice, no warranty line item. Default full ceramic kit prices at $370, which is low against typical retail for a ceramic sedan, so default overhead/labor assumptions need the owner to change them. I did not load the page in a browser; only the modules and page text tests were run.
evidence.domain: Compared against how installers actually buy and price: film is bought by roll width (36/40/60 in) and cut by linear foot, so area x waste% approximates but does not model real yield (a pro would check this first); flat per-vehicle pricing is indeed the industry norm and basing cost on panes, film tier and removal is sound. Per-pane install and removal minutes and $/sqft figures are plausible ballparks and are labeled as such in comments, but none is cited to a supplier price sheet or a timing study. Booth overhead is a flat $12 regardless of job length. Margin on price is the right convention. A practitioner would use it as a cost sanity check after replacing the constants, not sign it off as a bid tool.

defects.what: Blank numeric field is coerced to 0 with no error (e.g. installerRate '' prices labor at $0, giving 284.11 instead of 370.27), so an emptied input silently under-quotes.
Film waste is a flat percent of area; real yield depends on roll width and linear-foot cuts, and all rate constants are uncited ballparks.
Key market claim ('that is how the trade actually prices this work', the $180/$220/$250 list) is unsourced and the matching hypotheses are untested.
No front windshield strip, sunroof, or roll-width logic; quarter windows capped at 4 with no van/3rd-row glass.
llms.txt links use the retired github.io address, not https://marisstella.app/.
sitemap.xml and robots.txt point at https://example.invalid/ (unverified whether the deploy rewrites them).
Removal is all-or-nothing though the FAQ says only panes that already have tint need it; Boolean('false') is truthy; waste percent has no max.

verdict: The arithmetic is correct: three outputs recomputed by hand match to the cent, 107 tests pass, and a seeded margin-formula mutation was caught by 8 tests. The code is clean and the proposal feature goes beyond the calculator. It does not meet the bar because of claims (2): the central industry-practice claim is unsourced and unvalidated, llms.txt carries a retired URL, and sitemap/robots use an invalid host. A tint-shop owner would find the inputs plausible but uncited, the film-yield model simplistic (no roll width) and the glass coverage incomplete (no windshield strip or sunroof). Finished (completeness 3) but not bar-meeting; the correctness score rests on arithmetic I verified, not on the constants, which I could not source.
